spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The mathematical work is done by turning the relative position of support and Fourier-support projections into a commuting differential operator, then choosing a self-adjoint extension whose Sonin-space restriction has discrete negative spectrum. A Darboux-produced Dirac square root converts that spectrum into a quantity whose high-energy behavior can be compared with zeta zeros, suggesting an archimedean spectral component without identifying the individual zeros.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: On even L2(R), P_lambda cuts off to [-lambda,lambda] and its Fourier conjugate supplies the second projection. The prolate differential operator PW_lambda commutes with their angle operator; its natural self-adjoint extension is Fourier invariant and restricts to the Sonin space of functions, together with their Fourier transforms, vanishing on that interval. The source reports discrete negative spectrum there, a Darboux Dirac square root, and the same ultraviolet behavior as nontrivial zeta zeros, while the positive side corresponds asymptotically to trivial zeros.
directed.conceptual_reading: Commutation is the compression mechanism: a nonlocal two-projection geometry becomes accessible through a local differential operator. Restriction to Sonin space removes the directly time- and band-limited part, and the Dirac square root changes a comparison with squared ordinates into a first-order spectral comparison. This is evidence for an archimedean model at high energy, not a completed Hilbert-Polya realization.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The bridge is support projection plus Fourier-support projection -> angle operator -> commuting prolate differential operator -> self-adjoint Sonin restriction -> Darboux Dirac operator -> ultraviolet comparison with zeta ordinates. The scaling operator is cited as the conceptual link between the prolate formula and archimedean Weil positivity.
directed.boundary_or_failure: Only ultraviolet asymptotics are matched; neither individual eigenvalues, low zeros, nor one exact full zeta spectrum are obtained. The construction is reported for special lambda values, and ambiguity in the Dirac square root remains tied to differential Galois theory. The omitted plot supplies no accepted quantitative evidence.
directed.uncertainty: The extracted square-root and lambda typography is damaged, so exact normalizations and signs should not be inferred from this span. The claims from cited joint work are reported rather than proved here, and the figure cannot be recovered from normalized text.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: Wiener-Ikehara is the decisive bridge: after the pole at s=1 is isolated, boundary regularity of a transform becomes an asymptotic statement about a nonnegative monotone counting function. Applied to -zeta'/zeta, this converts the zero-free boundary line into psi(x) asymptotic to x and hence the Prime Number Theorem.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: The stated Tauberian theorem assumes a nonnegative increasing A, convergence of its transform for Re(s)>1, and continuous extension to Re(s)>=1 after subtracting c/(s-1); it concludes e^{-x}A(x) tends to c in the displayed convention. For primes, -zeta'(s)/zeta(s) is represented as a Mellin transform of the Chebyshev function psi. Nonvanishing of zeta on Re(s)=1 and its pole at 1 provide the required pole-subtracted boundary behavior, yielding psi(x)~x and then the Prime Number Theorem.
directed.conceptual_reading: The theorem separates a main singularity from a regular boundary remainder and interprets the singularity's residue as asymptotic mass. Nonnegativity and monotonicity are the rigidity that prevents transform boundary information from being defeated by cancellation.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The logarithmic derivative is the bridge object: it packages prime powers into an analytic transform. Pole subtraction exposes the main term, and Wiener-Ikehara transfers the resulting boundary regularity back to the growth of psi.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The Tauberian step does not establish the required nonvanishing of zeta on Re(s)=1; it consumes that input. The final elementary passage from psi(x)~x to the usual prime-counting asymptotic is asserted but not developed, and this note does not strengthen the zero-free result.
directed.uncertainty: The transform typography is extraction-fragmented and mixes Laplace and Mellin presentations, so exact conventions should be checked in the original. The logical implication and its hypotheses are nevertheless explicit in prose.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The span replaces pointwise behavior of zeta by two aggregate representations: Nevanlinna's characteristic records average positive logarithmic size plus pole density, while the Borchsenius-Jessen law records the vertical distribution of log zeta. The resulting r log r growth and full complex support describe abundance and variability without assuming RH or locating zeros.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: For meromorphic f, T(r,f)=m(r,f)+N(r,f), with m an angular average of log-plus magnitude and N the integrated pole count. The source reports T(r,zeta)~(1/pi)r log r. It also states that for fixed sigma>1/2, vertical averages of bounded continuous test functions of log zeta(sigma+it) converge to a probability measure; the measure is atomless and, for 1/2<sigma<1, has all of C as support, without assuming RH.
directed.conceptual_reading: These constructions trade exceptional pointwise behavior for stable distributional summaries. T compresses size and poles into one growth invariant, while weak convergence against test functions makes the multivalued and fluctuating log zeta accessible statistically. Full support signals that no open region of log-value space is excluded by the limiting law, not that zeros have been classified.
directed.representation_or_bridge: Nevanlinna theory bridges local magnitude and pole information to a global radial growth characteristic. The value-distribution theorem bridges long vertical sampling to a probability measure on C, with bounded continuous test functions providing the comparison interface.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The statements are reported technical context, not derived in the unit. They concern radial growth and vertical value distribution, not the location of zeta zeros, and full support does not imply RH or its negation. The support conclusion is restricted to the inner strip 1/2<sigma<1.
directed.uncertainty: Several displayed integrals are split by extraction, and the mechanism resolving branches of log zeta in the presence of zeros is not explained. The asymptotic, atomlessness, support, and lack of an RH assumption are clear prose-supported claims.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The key obstruction is loss of branch data: x^beta is unchanged when beta is shifted by 2 pi i/log x, but the integral it is supposed to represent is not. Replacing dependence on x^rho alone by Ei(rho log x) keeps the lifted logarithmic variable and its branch cut, repairing the zero term's representation.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: The passage tests a displayed identity under beta -> beta+2 pi i/log x. The exponent x^beta is periodic under that shift, whereas the left integral changes, so the two sides cannot be equal as written. It proposes the exponential integral Ei(z), with a branch cut from negative infinity to zero, and rewrites the explicit-formula zero contribution using Ei(rho log x) in a sum over zeros with positive imaginary part.
directed.conceptual_reading: Exponentiation quotients the beta log x coordinate by a period and therefore forgets information that the branch-sensitive integral retains. Moving to Ei on the logarithmic lift is not cosmetic notation: it restores the data needed to define the conditionally assembled zero contribution consistently.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The bridge is from the multiplicative expression x^rho to the additive lifted coordinate rho log x, followed by the branch-aware function Ei. The periodicity test acts as a falsifier for a representation that has compressed too aggressively.
directed.boundary_or_failure: This is a criticism and repair of notation in one source, not a claim that the classical explicit formula is false. Preserving branch information neither locates the zeros nor advances RH by itself.
directed.uncertainty: Extraction fragments the final formula and may have lost conjugation bars or other pairing notation, so its exact term-by-term typography requires the original. The periodicity defect and the proposed Ei(rho log x) replacement are explicit.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The module is the organizing map: the product of local absolute values descends to the semilocal quotient, relates its additive-measure L2 space to the multiplicative idele-class L2 space, and separates scaling from the kernel of the module. Taking kernel invariants then turns the general trace formula into the specialized form used earlier.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: For the semilocal ring A_S and quotient Y_S=A_S/Gamma, the product of local absolute values descends to Mod_S:Y_S->R_+*. The semilocal idele class group C_S acts by multiplication and embeds into Y_S as the orbit of 1; its complement has additive Haar measure zero. A Radon-Nikodym derivative yields a unitary identification w_S:L2(Y_S)->L2(C_S). The modulated group C_S is noncanonically isomorphic to R_+* x K_S, where K_S=ker Mod_S, and equation (22) is described as the K_S-invariant specialization of a general trace formula.
directed.conceptual_reading: The module records precisely how multiplicative motion rescales additive Haar measure. That correction makes the additive quotient and multiplicative orbit interchangeable at the Hilbert-space level up to null sets, while K_S-invariance removes norm-one directions and retains the scaling coordinate relevant to the specialized trace formula.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The bridge runs from local fields and their product norms to the quotient module, then from the full-measure idele-class orbit through a Radon-Nikodym unitary to L2(C_S), and finally through K_S invariants to the semilocal trace-formula interface.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The orbit embedding is only full measure, not equality of Y_S with C_S, and the product decomposition is explicitly noncanonical. This machinery specializes an existing trace formula; it is not an independent positivity theorem and does not supply the missing RH-critical estimate.
directed.uncertainty: Dense notation is partly degraded, equation (22) and the cited general trace formula are outside this packet, and the unit reports rather than derives the unitary identification. The maps, null-set qualification, and invariant specialization are nonetheless explicit.
